messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: web download links
parts:
Daniel and I were discussing how to organize the web pages.
With a beta release for 2 coming up and older versions, I
think we need a layer of indirection.

Something like a home page and then a per-product download page.
It's going to get too big with Python and then with MATLAB and maybe
even Stata. And all the versioning is too busy for the home page.

So I'd suggest something like this, which I'd be happy to code up
today before the 2.0 release-candidate goes out.

- Bob

=====================
...

-----------------
- Programming Guide
- Reference Manual
- Example Models

-----------------------------------

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] download multiple versions of R package?
parts:
We can set up another set of repository for rstan candidate release.  The drawback is that 
* it would be empty if we do not have candidate release
* if users set up the repo for the candidate release, they could not install the stable release as the version of bigger number would be picked up by R automatically.  To install the stable release, one way is to restart R. 

In addition, if we ask users to use library devtools to install R, we can ask users do something like the following webpage shows. If we use this way, we do not need to depend on the google code stuff any more. 

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] download multiple versions of R package?
parts:
On 10/15/13 6:10 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> We can set up another set of repository for rstan candidate release. The drawback is that
> * it would be empty if we do not have candidate release

In the future, we plan to stage things so we release Stan
first, and then RStan, Command-line Stan, and PyStan would all
work from that.

For now, we've tied in command-line Stan to Stan itself, but
RStan is decoupled in the sense that we only point to the install
instructions.

> * if users set up the repo for the candidate release, they could not install the stable release as the version of bigger
> number would be picked up by R automatically. To install the stable release, one way is to restart R.

If we have multiple releases up on your releases page,
then can you add some instructions for how users can
change either going forward or backward (that is, how
to start/stop/install in R). Thanks.

> In addition, if we ask users to use library devtools to install R, we can ask users do something like the following
> webpage shows. If we use this way, we do not need to depend on the google code stuff any more.
>
> https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases

This is great news. Should've read it before sending
out the last message. I'll delete Google Code.

- Bob
